notes:
Apps open inside a pane now.

Tapping one used to throw it fullscreen over the whole cockpit. A pane only ever received a window if it had already been configured with an app source, and nothing in the interface let you do that, so the split screen could not actually be used to open anything. The pane system was decorative. Tapping an app in a pane's drawer now hands that pane over to the app and launches its window into the pane's measured rectangle. Shortcuts open into whichever pane you touched last. The change is remembered, so the cockpit comes back the way you left it.

Long-press reaches the app menu again, on drawer tiles and on shortcuts. "Open fullscreen" and "Open in window" live in that menu, and it had quietly become unreachable when the tile that carried the long-press was removed a version ago. Fullscreen went with it.

There is a wallpaper, and the truck is on it by default. The photo ships inside the app, so there is nothing to set up: cropped to the panel and re-encoded, a 1024x1536 PNG at 2.25 MB becomes a 1920x1200 WebP at 95 KB. The source is portrait and the panel is landscape, so the crop is vertical and biased downward - a centre crop cut the roof off and showed mostly sky. The release APK goes from 6.56 to 6.67 MB for it. Settings > Display has three states: the bundled image, a plain background, or one you pick yourself, with a dim control.

The dim default was 0.72 and that was wrong, which the first render showed straight away. The photo is already nearly black, so dimming it that hard produced black and the wallpaper was invisible. Measured, its mean luminance is 0.010 against the design background's 0.0036 - three times brighter, still very dark - and full-contrast text clears 9.2:1 over its brightest areas undimmed. The default dim is now 0.30.

The only thing that ever struggled was muted text, at 3.2:1. The fix was not to dim the picture into nothing, but to stop putting muted text on a photograph: labels in a see-through pane use the full text colour.

Cards stay fully opaque. Every contrast figure in this design was measured against a flat near-black field, and a photograph behind a readout makes all of those numbers fiction. Only panes holding the app drawer, or holding nothing, are transparent - that is the one place on this screen with enough open area for a backdrop to be seen at all. The wallpaper changes the margins and the space around cards, not what sits behind text.

If you pick your own image it is downsampled to the panel as it decodes. A phone photo is commonly 4000px wide and decoding one at full size costs about 48 MB; the deck reports roughly 600 MB free of 1.8 GB, measured on the device this week. The picker takes a persistable permission on the file, so your choice survives a reboot rather than coming back blank.

Settings' section tabs are white rather than cyan, so the bottom bar keeps the one accent-coloured element on any screen.

The wallpaper snapshot test was a lie and has been replaced. layoutlib cannot decode WebP, so the decode returned nothing and the "wallpaper" render was identical to the plain one, pixel for pixel, and would have passed forever. It now composites a flat mid-grey around fifteen times brighter than the shipped photo. That is a far harsher test than the real thing, and what it actually proves is the compositing: the image draws, the dim applies, cards stay opaque, the drawer pane shows through. 18 tests pass.

Still to check in the truck, unchanged from the last release: whether a window can be parked off-screen when a pane is swiped away from an app, and whether the divider between two panes can be grabbed in the gap between two windows.
